title: This Whole Forest Is ONE Tree 🌳
description:
This whole forest you're standing in is ONE tree. The real tree is underground: every trunk is a sprout off the same roots, about 47,000 of them. Same roots, same DNA: hug one and you've hugged them all. That's why each autumn the whole forest turns gold at the same time. And it weighs about 6,000 tonnes, about forty big blue whales... of tree.
One tree or a forest: what did you guess?

The science: Pando is a single male quaking aspen (Populus tremuloides) in Fishlake National Forest, Utah. It spread by sending up new stems (suckers) from its roots, so its roughly 47,000 trunks (a 1970s count) over 106 acres are one genetic individual: DNA tests of the stems find one genotype (DeWoody et al. 2008; Mitton & Grant 1996). The trunks of one aspen clone change colour together in autumn, which is how you can pick out clones on a hillside (US Forest Service). Its weight, roots included, is estimated at about 6,000 tonnes (over 13 million lb: Grant 1993); a big Antarctic blue whale weighs about 150 tonnes (NOAA). Nobody knows Pando's exact age: thousands of years is the safe answer (the '80,000 years' you may read is not supported). Bonus: "Pando" is Latin for "I spread", and the dark "eyes" on aspen bark are scars where old branches fell off. (The trunks' eyes opening is a joke.)
